text: According to the chapter, which of the following best distinguishes Nextflow from Snakemake for bioinformatics pipelines?
choices: Snakemake cannot use containers, while Nextflow requires Docker for every process
Snakemake only supports R scripts, while Nextflow only supports shell commands
Nextflow is better suited to cloud platforms with stronger containerization, while Snakemake is more Pythonic and favored for HPC/SLURM environments
Nextflow cannot automatically infer a DAG of task dependencies, unlike Snakemake
explanation: The chapter contrasts Nextflow's cloud-oriented design (AWS Batch, Google Cloud) and strong containerization with Snakemake's Pythonic, readable syntax that is well-suited to HPC/SLURM clusters. Snakemake does support containers via a `container:` directive, so that option is false; both tools can execute shell commands or scripts in any language, so the language restriction is false; and both frameworks automatically build an execution DAG from input/output dependencies, so that option is false too.
